summary: B is preferable because it explicitly implements required input validation and preserves the existing Add test while adding clearer multipart and retry coverage. Both patches share a significant contract violation: Upload bypasses FilesService.Add through a new private helper, and both change Add to eagerly buffer every caller-provided body.
reasons: B explicitly rejects an empty filename and nil content before multipart construction; A relies on undocumented behavior of multipartbody.NewFile.

B retains TestFilesService_Add and adds separate tests for multipart encoding, Add replayability, and retrying an Upload sourced from an os.File. A replaces the existing Add test and combines several Upload concerns into one test.
B's separation of encoding and retry tests makes failures easier to diagnose and review.
Both correctly reuse internal/multipartbody.NewFile and verify the required field name, uploaded filename, content, and retry behavior.
risks_a: Upload calls s.add directly rather than routing through FilesService.Add as explicitly required.
Add is changed from streaming the supplied reader to eagerly reading it into memory, which does not preserve its existing behavior.

There are no visible validation or source-reader-error tests, and validation is not explicit in Upload itself broader than helper behavior inferred nowhere in the diff text provided here under the user instruction to use only material in the message. The sentence currently says relies undocumented. Keep no inference. Could say no explicit checks. Good. Should avoid mention source helper behavior maybe fair. Need ensure
risks_b: Upload also bypasses FilesService.Add through s.add, violating the required single path for option handling, request construction, decoding, and errors.
Add is unnecessarily changed to buffer all custom bodies, altering lower-level streaming behavior.
The new tests omit the contract-required validation and source-reader-error cases.
